notes: Values are moment.js's own lb locale, which is the right source here because this project's locale set is a mirror of moment's. Four things. FIRST, monthsInDate is deliberately IDENTICAL to months: Luxembourgish does not inflect the month inside a date, so 5. Abrëll 2026 uses the plain name. SECOND, the date is written 05.04.2026 with FULL STOPS, the German way, and the long form takes an ordinal point after the day — D. MMMM YYYY, '5. Abrëll 2026'. The same country writes 05/04/2026 in French on the form next to it. THIRD, the time is written with a bare hour and the word Auer after it — moment's lb LT is 'H:mm [Auer]', so 14:30 Auer, and no leading zero on the hour. FOURTH and most important for anyone extending this: moment's lb locale contains a function called eifelerRegelAppliesToNumber, which exists because relative time in Luxembourgish changes the SPELLING of the preposition according to the sound that follows it — 'an 10 Deeg' but 'a 5 Deeg', because 'fënnef' begins with f and 'zéng' with z. That is the Eifel Rule (see word/verb.txt), it is the only rule of its kind in moment's whole locale corpus, and any formatter that renders Luxembourgish relative time without it produces text that is wrong in a way a native reader sees instantly. The currency is the euro, written 1.234,56 € with a full stop for thousands and a comma for decimals when the text is in Luxembourgish or German, and 1 234,56 € when the same office writes in French.
